fields.body: Five consecutive terms in the Bihar Legislative Assembly — Patna West in 2006, then Bankipur in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025.
Cabinet Minister in the Government of Bihar, holding Road Construction, Urban Development & Housing, and Law & Justice.
Bihar state president and national general secretary of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha; party in-charge for Sikkim and Chhattisgarh.
Appointed National Working President in December 2025 and elected National President on 20 January 2026 — the youngest to hold the office and the first from Bihar.

bioSections.title: Introduction
bioSections.body: Nitin Nabin is the National President of the Bharatiya Janata Party and a five-time member of the Bihar Legislative Assembly from Bankipur. He has held three portfolios in the Government of Bihar and has worked in the party organisation for nearly two decades.

bioSections.title: Early life
bioSections.body: Born on 23 May 1980 in Ranchi, in present-day Jharkhand. He is the son of Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha, a four-time legislator from Patna West.

bioSections.title: Education
bioSections.body: Public reporting records that he has studied to Intermediate level, Class 12. No further verified detail is available, and none has been recorded here.

bioSections.title: Entry into public life
bioSections.body: He entered politics as an active member of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha. In 2006, at twenty-six, he contested the by-election for Patna West left vacant by his father's death and won by a margin of nearly 60,000 votes.

bioSections.title: Electoral journey
bioSections.body: Patna West in 2006, then Bankipur in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025 — five consecutive wins. He defeated Luv Sinha by 39,036 votes in 2020 and Rekha Kumari by 51,936 votes in 2025, when he polled 98,299 votes.

bioSections.title: Organisational work
bioSections.body: He was state president of the Bihar Yuva Morcha until 2019 and national general secretary of the wing. He was later made party in-charge for Sikkim and election in-charge for Chhattisgarh, where he led the 2023 assembly campaign.

bioSections.title: Government responsibilities
bioSections.body: Minister of Road Construction from 9 February 2021 to 9 August 2022. Re-appointed a minister on 15 March 2024, holding Law & Justice until 26 February 2025 alongside Road Construction and Urban Development & Housing.

bioSections.title: National role
bioSections.body: In December 2025 the Parliamentary Board appointed him National Working President — the youngest in the party's history and the first from Bihar. He resigned from the Bihar cabinet the following day, citing the principle of one man, one post.

bioSections.title: Current responsibilities
bioSections.body: On 20 January 2026 he was elected National President, unopposed, at the party headquarters in New Delhi, having been the sole candidate with 37 valid sets of nomination papers. He has since made organisational visits to West Bengal, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh.
